findings.title: appendStep writes and publishes the step with its cost, then charges; when the charge throws, the receipt stays with no charge behind it
findings.scenario: A worker calls appendStep(id,'tool','search: x',{tool:'search',cost:{dollars:0.01}}). writeStep commits the step and publishes step.appended. Then addSpend -> trace.addCost rejects (ledger refuses, database drops between the two transactions). The task goes to 'failed'. The page and every later snapshot show a search block with '$0.01' on it, while task.ownCost, snapshot.spend and the ledger are 0. The comment in worker.ts says 'a step's receipt and the task's cost cannot disagree'; they can. The two writes are two separate transactions in PgTrace (appendStep withTransaction, addCost withTransaction).
findings.evidence: Probe test on PgTrace with recordSpend = () => Promise.reject(new Error('ledger refused')) printed: PG receipt [{"cost":{"dollars":0.01},"tool":"search"}] ownCost { dollars: 0 } failed. Same on MemoryTrace with addCost rejecting and demoWorker: 'P1 receipts 3 spend { dollars: 0 } statuses [ ended, failed, failed, failed ] cost events 0'. Code: kernel.ts 178 `await this.writeStep(taskId, kind, text, kept);` then 180-182 `await this.addSpend(...)`. A fix that holds: charge first and write the step second, or one Trace method that does both in one transaction.

findings.title: delegate() leaves every child 'queued' for the life of the process when the delegate step cannot be written
findings.scenario: delegate() opens 3 children and publishes task.opened for each, then awaits writeStep(parent,'delegate',...). If that write rejects (database error, or the new jsonb insert refuses the payload), delegate() rejects before runBounded. run()'s catch sets only the parent to 'failed'. The 3 readers stay 'queued': the call tree shows three tasks that never start, until the user presses stop or the server restarts and restore() marks them stopped. Before this commit the delegate step was written before any child existed, so this failure point is new.
findings.evidence: Probe: MemoryTrace whose appendStep rejects for kind 'delegate', demoWorker, after kernel.idle(): P2 statuses [ 'lead:failed', 'reader:queued', 'reader:queued', 'reader:queued' ]. Code: kernel.ts 207-217, no try/catch around writeStep, no status change for the opened children on the error path.

findings.title: Terminal output with a NUL character or a lone surrogate makes the jsonb insert throw in Postgres, while MemoryTrace accepts it
findings.scenario: A 'run' tool step carries detail.output from a real process. Binary output holds U+0000; an output cut with slice() can end on half a surrogate pair. JSON.stringify escapes both as � / \ud83d, and `$4::jsonb` refuses both. appendStep rejects, the worker run throws, the task ends 'failed', and the step is lost. No test sees it because MemoryTrace keeps the object as given, and traceContract's output sample has neither character.
findings.evidence: Probe on PgTrace (Postgres 17 at :54329): detail {output:'a'+String.fromCharCode(0)+'b'} -> 'nul THROWS unsupported Unicode escape sequence'; {output:'a'+String.fromCharCode(0xd83d)} -> 'surrogate THROWS invalid input syntax for type json'. Code: pgTrace.ts 200 `[taskId, kind, text, detail ? JSON.stringify(detail) : null]`.

findings.title: StepDetail has no size bound and no shape check: one step can put megabytes into every snapshot and every socket frame, and a wrong shape is stored and sent as given
findings.scenario: Only cost (recordable) and childTaskIds are checked. A worker that passes a 20 MB output gets it stored; the step.appended event carries all of it to every socket, and every later GET /api/sessions/:id and session.snapshot frame carries it again. A worker that passes rows:'nope' or durationMs:NaN (the steering slice will build detail from model output) gets it stored; Postgres returns durationMs:null and rows as a string, both outside the contract. On the page, parts.tsx 145-147 calls detail.rows.map on a non-empty string and throws in render; took(null) draws '0 ms'.
findings.evidence: Probe on PgTrace: 'rows-string OK -> {"rows":"nope"}', 'nan OK -> {"durationMs":null}', 'big OK' for a 20 MiB output, then 'snapshot bytes 20972373'. Probe on the kernel with MemoryTrace and a 5 MiB output: task status 'ended', 'snapshot bytes 5243481', 'event bytes 5243057'. grep for maxPayload / a length check in kernel.ts, pgTrace.ts, memoryTrace.ts: none; the only limit in the server is Fastify bodyLimit for requests (core/http/server.ts 59), which does not cover worker output. One bound on the serialized detail in Kernel.appendStep (truncate output, cap rows) plus Array.isArray / Number.isFinite checks covers both traces.

findings.title: LUMEN_DEMO_PACE_MS accepts a blank string as 0 and accepts '1e3' and '0x10'
findings.scenario: LUMEN_DEMO_PACE_MS=' ' (a space left in a .env line) gives Number(' ') = 0, which passes the integer check. The demo runs with no pace and no error, which is the case the function exists to refuse. '1e3' gives 1000 and '0x10' gives 16.
findings.evidence: node: " " -> 0 accepted; "1e3" -> 1000 accepted; "0x10" -> 16 accepted; "10001" and "4s" rejected. Code: main.ts 130-133 checks only `raw === ''` before Number(raw). A /^\d+$/ test on raw closes it.

checked_and_fine: Order on the socket in a fan-out: task.opened x3, then step.appended/delegate, then the children's task.status. Probe printed: task.opened task.status step.appended/thinking task.opened task.opened task.opened step.appended/delegate task.status task.status. The delegate step comes before any child event other than task.opened, and the children it names already exist on the page.

A page that joins mid-run: the web reducer drops a step.appended whose (taskId, index) is already in the snapshot (apps/web/src/core/api.ts 159), and it keeps the whole event, so detail is not lost. The older race (snapshot read before a step, published after it) is not changed by this commit.

Budget refuses at fan-out: ask() returns before any child is opened and before writeStep, so DelegationRefused leaves no child and no delegate step (kernel.ts 201-202). Budget refuses at task-open: the child is set stopped or waiting and gets a 'Not run' step; it is not left queued.

restore() after a crash between opening the children and writing the delegate step: trace.openTasks() returns the queued children and the running parent, all become 'stopped'. No delegate step names them; treeRows draws them from parentId, and childrenByStep gives unnamed children only to a delegate step without childTaskIds, so nothing is mis-assigned. The children show in the call tree and under no delegate block.

A stop that arrives between the opening of the children and the delegate step: probe gave statuses [stopped x4]; run(child, onlyIfQueued) returns for each child, none runs. The delegate and reply steps are still written on the stopped parent; this is the same as before the commit.
Bad cost: recordable() runs before writeStep, so a negative amount writes neither a step nor a charge (covered by the branch's test, and read in kernel.ts 177).
A worker cannot name childTaskIds: appendStep throws before any write (kernel.ts 174). An empty array [] passes the truthiness check? No: [] is truthy, so it throws too.
undefined fields in detail: JSON.stringify drops them; {} is stored as '{}' and read back as detail:{} (truthy), MemoryTrace does the same. Null column reads back as absent. Both traces agree here.
Migration 008: nullable jsonb column with no default, so it is a metadata-only change on Postgres 17; the down migration drops it. Old rows read back with no detail key (toStep).
The jsonb write uses a bound parameter with ::jsonb; no SQL is built from detail. The row lock on the task still serializes max(index)+1.
main.ts imports demoWorker through modules/session/index.js, the public index. composeApp passes options.worker through; tests build the app without it and get demoWorker() with paceMs 0.

demoWorker pace: setTimeout only when paceMs > 0; durationMs is measured. With maxParallel 3 the three readers pace in parallel. There is no abort on stop, so a stopped reader finishes its current wait (at most 10 s by the env bound) and then writes its steps onto a stopped task; this matches the behaviour before the commit.

Full server suite in a throwaway worktree with DATABASE_URL set: 44 files, 524 tests passed on the second run. The first run showed 2 failed tests while another worktree (/tmp/wf-tests) used the same Postgres; I did not capture their names and they did not recur, so treat it as an unverified flake under load, not as a finding. Worktree /tmp/wf-server is removed; the main working tree is untouched.
